title: India just finished a 2,843-kilometre railway built to carry nothing but freight
sources: Free Press Journal, September 2026 - Western Dedicated Freight Corridor Fully Operational, Boosting India's Logistics Network
Maritime Gateway, September 2026 - PM Modi Completes Western Freight Corridor
caption:
India just finished a railway built for one purpose only: cargo. No passengers, no mixed traffic - just freight, moving faster than ever before.

On September 8, 2026, Prime Minister Modi dedicated the final sections of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor, making the full network operational - 2,843 km combined across the Eastern corridor (Ludhiana to Sonnagar, 1,337 km) and Western corridor (Dadri to Jawaharlal Nehru Port, 1,506 km). Days after opening, the Western corridor set a new record: 431 trains interchanged in a single day, breaking its own record from two weeks earlier.

Cargo used to wait behind passenger trains on the same tracks. Now it has its own railway, built to move at industrial speed.
